title: Well-definedness of the genus
statement:
Let $k$ be a field and $X$ a smooth projective curve over $k$ which is
geometrically irreducible. Then
$\dim_kH^1(X,\mathcal{O}_X)<\infty$.

proof.text: Choose an algebraic closure $\bar k$ of $k$ using [lem-pc-algebraic-closure-exists-unique], and form $X_{\bar k}$ by [def-pc-base-change]. Since $X$ is a smooth projective curve [def-pc-smooth-projective-curve], its structure morphism is smooth and projective and $X$ is a curve [def-pc-curve]. Smoothness persists by [lem-pc-proper-base-change](2), and projectivity persists by [lem-pc-projective-base-change]. Its dimension is exactly $1$ by [lem-pc-dim-base-change]. The structure morphism of $X$ is proper by [lem-pc-projective-proper], hence that of $X_{\bar k}$ is proper by [lem-pc-proper-base-change](1), so it is separated and of finite type by [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Smoothness of $X$ over $k$ gives geometrically reduced fibres by [sbc-lem-smooth-geometrically-reduced]; the fibre over the unique point of $\operatorname{Spec}k$ is $X$, hence $X_{\bar k}$ is reduced. Geometric irreducibility [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible] makes $X_{\bar k}$ irreducible and nonempty; reducedness and irreducibility make it integral by [def-pc-integral-scheme]. Thus it satisfies every condition in [def-pc-curve] and [def-pc-smooth-projective-curve] over $\bar k$. Apply [lem-pc-curve-coherent-finiteness] to the coherent structure sheaf $\mathcal O_{X_{\bar k}}$ at $i=1$ to obtain finite-dimensional $H^1(X_{\bar k},\mathcal O_{X_{\bar k}})$ over $\bar k$.

source.place: Tags 02H2 (smooth base change), 01WF (H-projective base change), 01K5 (quasi-compact base change), and 01W4 (proper base change); dimension: Tag 00P3; geometrically reduced: Tag 056T; integral: Tag 01ON

proof.text: Since $X$ is a smooth projective curve [def-pc-smooth-projective-curve], it is proper over $k$ by [lem-pc-projective-proper]. The field extension $k\to\bar k$ is flat, and $\mathcal O_X$ is quasi-coherent; its pullback to $X_{\bar k}$ is the structure sheaf $\mathcal O_{X_{\bar k}}$. Thus [lem-sc-flat-base-change-coherent], applied with $i=1$, $k'=\bar k$, and $\mathcal F=\mathcal O_X$, identifies $H^1(X_{\bar k},\mathcal O_{X_{\bar k}})$ with $H^1(X,\mathcal O_X)\otimes_k\bar k$.

If $H^1(X,\mathcal O_X)$ were infinite-dimensional, any finite linearly independent subset would remain linearly independent after tensoring with the field extension $\bar k/k$. The resulting arbitrarily large independent subsets would contradict the finite dimension of $H^1(X_{\bar k},\mathcal O_{X_{\bar k}})$ from step 1. Hence $H^1(X,\mathcal O_X)$ is finite-dimensional over $k$.
